column1: # Edges of the rules OpenVerse took from Epic's verdicts on followup-book3 (#724): type names that differ only in case, packing beside a named parameter, the measured name lengths and parametric mutable data. Compile first; what OpenVerse does is in each probe's header and in note (Lean and C agreeing); Epic's outcome in epic_outcome (- where not yet compiled). Run the long-ident probes alone (single mode); no struct name here comes near the 1016 characters that crashed the editor.

column7: OpenVerse: refused. Asks the same of a class cc and an enum CC. OpenVerse refuses it (#724). If Epic admits it, it prints lower 1

OpenVerse: ran. Control-like edge: a class cc and a module function CC(). OpenVerse measures types against types and functions against functions only, and admits it: lower 1 | upper 2 If Epic refuses it, a type and a function collide too.
OpenVerse: refused. Asks the same of a class cc and an interface CC. OpenVerse refuses it (#724). If Epic admits it, it prints lower 1
OpenVerse: ran. Control-like edge: a class cc in module mm and a class CC at the top level, two scopes. OpenVerse admits it: lower 1 | upper 2 If Epic refuses it, types collide across modules.
OpenVerse: refused. Asks the same of a class cc and a struct CC. OpenVerse refuses it (#724). If Epic admits it, it prints lower 1 | upper 2
OpenVerse: refused. Asks the same of two enums, ee and EE. OpenVerse refuses it (#724). If Epic admits it, it prints compared
OpenVerse: refused. Asks the same of two interfaces, ii and II. OpenVerse refuses it (#724). If Epic admits it, it prints defined

OpenVerse: refused. Asks whether two structs of one scope whose names differ only in case collide, as two classes do (UEFN 43.12 refuses cc and CC, 9002 "Found existing type 'CC'", followup-book3/case-collision-classes). OpenVerse takes every type alike and refuses it ("the types ss and SS have names that differ only in case", #724). If Epic admits it, it prints lower 1 | upper 2

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the 3509 rule (#724): F(1, 2) of F(X:t, ?E:int = 0 where t:type), several arguments for a generic parameter beside a named one. Epic refuses them for a tuple and an array parameter (followup-book2/overload-tuple-named-call, followup-book3/array-named-pack). OpenVerse still packs them into t's tuple and prints result 0 If Epic refuses it (3509), a generic parameter beside a named one takes no several arguments either.

OpenVerse: refused. Edge of the length rules (#724): a module constant of 1005 characters, which OpenVerse limits as a field and a local (1004) and refuses. If Epic admits it, it prints result 42 Run it alone (single mode).

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the length rules (#724): an enum of 1023 characters. OpenVerse admits it (an identifier of at most 1024) and prints compared If Epic refuses it, an enum's name is limited as a class's or less. Run it alone (single mode).

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the length rules (#724): a module function of 990 characters, the most measured without parameters, with a parameter X:int. OpenVerse admits it and prints result 42 If Epic refuses it, parameters lower a function's limit. Run it alone (single mode).

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the length rules (#724): an interface of 1023 characters, the most a class may have. OpenVerse limits classes and structs only (1023), and admits it: defined If Epic refuses it, an interface's derived name is longer. Run it alone (single mode).

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the length rules (#724): a method F(P:int), with a parameter, in a class of 976 characters (977 together, within the 987 measured for methods without parameters). Epic refuses Function(Param:int) there (3655, followup-book2/long-ident-mangled) and admits Function() (followup-book3/long-ident-mangled-no-params). OpenVerse admits it and prints method 7 If Epic refuses it, a parameter alone takes the method past the limit. Run it alone (single mode).

OpenVerse: refused. Edge of the length rules (#724): a parameter of 1005 characters; Epic refuses a field and a local of 1005 (3655) and admits 1004. OpenVerse takes the same limit for a parameter and refuses it. If Epic admits it, it prints result 42 Run it alone (single mode).

OpenVerse: refused. Edge of the 3552 rule (#724): F(X:[]c(t) where t:type), the class inside an array type. OpenVerse finds the class anywhere in the type and refuses it. If Epic admits it, it prints length 1

OpenVerse: refused. Edge of the 3552 rule (#724): a method of another class with an implicit type parameter of its own, Use(X:c(u) where u:type). OpenVerse refuses it as it does a function. If Epic admits it, it prints result 1

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the 3552 rule (#724): a struct s(t) whose field holds c(t), with c's var Data:t; F(X:t where t:type):s(t). Epic refuses it through a class's field (followup-book3/parametric-var-where-nested). OpenVerse follows classes' fields only and admits it: data 2 If Epic refuses it (3552), a struct's fields count too.
